svg.title: claude-bulkhead: four Claude Code sessions sharing one machine without hurting each other
svg.desc: Animated loop of four Claude Code sessions, each in its own git worktree of acme-web, on one machine with a status strip for RAM, disk I/O and listening ports. port-guard moves a second dev server from port 3000 to 3001. kill-guard blocks pkill node and the agent restarts its own server by PID. disk-guard blocks a parallel du over the home folder and the agent measures one folder. checkout-guard blocks git add -A in a tree another session is editing and the agent commits only its own two files. bulkhead-slot makes a third heavy job wait for RAM, then runs it. The loop ends on bulkhead scan: 24 commands in 13 sessions would have been stopped, with up to 4 sessions running at once. The machine stays healthy throughout.

g.text: Four Claude Code sessions. One machine.
Two dev servers, one port. The second one moves.
pkill node would take down every session's server.
A parallel disk scan, cut down to one folder.
git add -A would sweep in another session's edits.
The third heavy job waits for RAM, then runs.
bulkhead scan shows what it would have stopped.

text.tspan: each in its own git worktree

g.text: Each session thinks it has the machine to itself.
bulkhead's hooks check every shell command before it runs, and say what to run instead.
[bulkhead] port-guard: port 3000 is already used by another Claude session (~/code/acme-web).
If you start yours anyway, requests to localhost:3000 reach the other project. Port 3001 is free:
[bulkhead] kill-guard: pkill/killall matches every process with that name
Killing by name takes down their dev servers, test runs and builds, and can end your own session.
Stop only the processes you started, by PID: lsof -ti :3002, then kill <pid>
[bulkhead] disk-guard: `ls ~ | xargs -P 10 du -sh` runs disk scans through xargs -P.
Several scans at once keep the disk at 100% and freeze the other sessions.
Run one du at a time, in the foreground: du -sh <one folder>.
Bash(git add -A && git commit -m "docs: setup guide")
[bulkhead] checkout-guard: `git add -A` stages every change in ~/code/acme-web (7 files),
and another Claude session works in the same tree (pid 4120).
Some of those changes are probably its half-finished work, and they would go into your commit.
Bash(git commit -m "docs: setup guide" -- README.md docs/setup.md)
[bulkhead-slot] waiting: free 7.0 GB - this job 3 GB = 4.0 GB, below the 5 GB floor
read 14 transcripts (338 KB), 14 sessions, 527 shell commands
overlap up to 4 sessions running at once
sessions running at once, at most
